Run and manage CPN-based workflow factories.

What:
CPN-based workflow factory CLI for running factories, submitting work, and inspecting live sessions.

How to use:
Run you run --work ./docs/examples/startup-work.json to start the exact Current Factory at ./factory/factory.json with explicit Work and no local server.
Use you server for continuous, non-resumable hosting of the Current Factory API and dashboard. For restart-surviving hosting, use you run --with-server --continuously --record <path>. Add --with-server or --with-site to host one run. See you <cmd> --help for subcommand details.

Agents:
Start with you docs agents for orientation, you submit or you submit batch to enqueue work, and you session list to confirm a live factory.
Run you docs for all packaged reference topics. Use --verbose or --debug for stderr diagnostics; full policy in you docs.

Usage:
  you [flags]
  you [command]

Examples:
  # Start the default Codex-backed Factory with explicit Work.
  you run --work ./docs/examples/startup-work.json

  # Agent orientation and command matrix.
  you docs agents

Available Commands:
  completion      Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  config          Configuration command guide
  docs            Print packaged markdown reference topics
  factory         Inspect and manage factory definitions
  help            Help about any command
  init            Configure provider and model defaults
  metrics         Inspect recorded Factory Runtime metrics
  models          Run local inference for language, speech, voice, and embeddings
  providers       Discover provider capabilities
  run             Load workflow and run the factory engine
  server          Serve the Current Factory API and dashboard
  session         List, open, and close factory sessions on a running host
  submit          Submit work to a running factory
  work            Inspect work from a running factory
  worker-sessions Inspect Worker Sessions
  workers         Manage worker execution integrations

Flags:
  -d, --debug           emit lower-level command diagnostics where supported (implies --verbose)
  -h, --help            help for you
      --json            emit structured JSON on stdout for supported commands; diagnostics remain on stderr
      --remote          execute a supported operation through a running You server; does not wait, follow, continue, or start a listener
      --server string   factory API base URI (http:// or https://) for HTTP client commands and remote placement; listener-owning commands use --listen host:port for explicit local binds, while local --server binding remains a warned compatibility path (default "http://localhost:7437")
  -v, --verbose         emit concise command diagnostics to stderr
      --version         version for you

Use "you [command] --help" for more information about a command.
